chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from Ahmad ibn Ziyad, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man upon whom death is approaching, and he has slaves belonging exclusively to himself and slaves in partnership with another man. Then he states in his bequest: 'My slaves are free, except my slaves who are in partnership.'
So he عليه السلام wrote: 'They are to be appraised against him; if his wealth can bear it, then they are free.'

key_terms.الشِّرْكَةِ: joint ownership or partnership in property
key_terms.الْوَفَاةُ: death or the approach of death
key_terms.يُقَوَّمُونَ: they are appraised or assigned a monetary value

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a dying man bequeaths freedom for slaves who are jointly owned with another person?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning a dying man's bequest to free slaves, including those jointly owned with another person. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the jointly owned slaves are to be appraised against the deceased's estate, and if his wealth is sufficient to cover their value, they are then set free.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5497 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr Al-Bazanti narrated from Ahmad ibn Ziyad who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (as) about a man who was on his deathbed and had slaves solely for himself and others jointly owned with another person. In his will, he stated, "My slaves are free, except for those who are in partnership."
Imam (as) wrote in response: "They should be appraised against his estate, and if his wealth can cover it, then they are free."
